name: Productivity & Personal Workspace

designIntent.primaryGoal: Help users capture, prioritize and complete work with low friction.
designIntent.visualThesis: A quiet workspace that keeps the next useful action obvious.

visualDirection.density: medium; allow a denser compact mode when users manage many items
visualDirection.surfaces: subtle separation, few elevation levels, strong selected and focused states
visualDirection.colorIntent: mostly neutral structure with semantic status and a contextual accent
visualDirection.typography: readable UI scale; clear distinction between task title, metadata and due date
visualDirection.motion: small feedback for completion, reordering and navigation; respect reduced motion

layout.pattern: persistent navigation + contextual list/board + optional detail pane
layout.spacing: consistent and scannable; list rows need adequate hit areas
layout.responsive: single-column navigation and detail views on narrow screens

avoid: too many panels competing for attention
overly playful feedback that delays completion

accessibility.keyboard: support predictable navigation and visible focus
accessibility.focus: selected, focused and completed states must be distinguishable
accessibility.reducedMotion: reordering and transitions need non-animated alternatives

antiPatterns: tiny drag handles without keyboard alternatives
notes: Let density respond to workflow complexity instead of treating minimalism as a universal goal.

aiGuidance.primaryFlow: Capture → clarify → prioritize → schedule or group → complete → review.
prioritize: The inbox, current list or project that holds the user's work
The next actionable item and its state
Due date, priority, owner and context only when they affect a decision
confirmOrMarkUnknown: Whether data is personal, shared or team-owned
Meaning of priority, due dates, recurring tasks and completion
Calendar availability and sync behavior before implying they are live
avoidByDefault: Dashboard widgets unrelated to a real task
acceptanceChecks: Quick capture is reachable from the primary workspace
Selection and detail remain understandable on narrow screens
Empty, overdue, completed, offline and saving states are distinct

compositionEscapes.when: The main job is processing incoming tasks, notes, requests or reminders.
compositionEscapes.composition: Make the inbox the primary surface; pair a compact triage queue with one detail area and explicit actions to defer, schedule, assign or complete.
contentRequirements: Clear distinction between unprocessed and processed items
Metadata relevant to the next action
Recoverable actions and undo where needed

compositionEscapes.when: Time, sequencing, availability or dependencies are central to the user's task.
compositionEscapes.composition: Use a calendar or timeline as the main canvas with a selected-item detail view; provide a list alternative for dense or narrow views.
contentRequirements: Reliable dates, durations and timezone rules

compositionEscapes.when: Users repeatedly scan, edit and compare many records or tasks.
compositionEscapes.composition: Anchor the screen in a readable list or table and show selected-item details contextually; navigate explicitly between list and detail on small screens.
contentRequirements: Stable item labels and useful sorting/filtering
Visible selected state and preserved list context
avoid: One oversized card per row when a list is clearer
